text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Danish authorities are now tightening rules for deporting for Bosnians, Tamils and Somalis on the grounds that some parts of their home countries are now so peaceful that they can be send back there, even though they came from other parts of their home countries when leaving for Denmark.

--- Transport minister Jan Troejborg and Crown Prince Frederik have left for Brazil on an official visit to promote Danish business and meet influential Brazilians, among them former football player, now sports minister, Pele.
--- New figures from Denmark's statistics Office show that 16,274 new companies were set up in 1994, an increase of 780 new companies -- or 5 percent -- compared to the year before.

--- Economics minister Marianne Jelved will fight to retain Denmark's taxfree trade until the year 2004 at a meeting with the rest of EU's economics ministers on November 11. Jelved argues that Denmark is a special case and that abolition of all taxfree trade will cost Denmark large profits and many jobs.
--- Telecommunications company Tele Danmark is to lower its standard domestic tariff by an average 1.5 percent amid a complete overhaul of its price structure.

--- Denmark will lose agricultural exports worth 20-25 billion crowns if the U.S.A succeeds in limiting EU countries' and especially Denmark's access to a large number of markets in the developing world via the world trade organisation WTO.
